cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: Gate 1/2/3 were implemented serially in a single worktree without consulting ADR-PD-001, the accepted parallel-development protocol in effect since v1.7.3.
impact: Gate 4/5/6 had to be re-planned as a 3+1 wave; the earlier serial work could not benefit from independent evaluation or lane isolation.
lesson: Before starting a version, grep docs/superpowers/specs for accepted ADRs and start each devline from a frozen Context Pack; the discipline surfaces binding constraints the memory index does not.

cause: The ETS 1.0 contract had no time_index_semantics field, so it would have blocked VIXCLS, a trading-day series whose weekend gaps are not missing data.
impact: Lane B flagged that the Notebook's alternative model was unusable on the very dataset v1.8.0 shipped with; contract amended to 1.1 with a backward-compatible optional field.
lesson: When adding a model that shares data with an existing pack, mirror the existing pack's index and sample vocabulary in the Contract Sprint, or the two models cannot be compared on one series.

cause: The canonical ETS fixture carried aic and log_likelihood implying six parameters but a bic implying 5.897; the numbers could not come from one likelihood.
impact: Because every lane mocks against the canonical fixture, an incoherent fixture would teach three lanes to accept an incoherent packet. Found by independent evaluation and repaired by Integration.
lesson: Hand-authored numeric fixtures must be checked for internal arithmetic identity between AIC, BIC, log-likelihood and the parameter count before they become a shared lock.

cause: NotebookOptionRevision.from_dict read named keys and silently dropped extras while its two sibling packets rejected them; a lane could smuggle an unversioned field and the packet would still validate.
impact: This is the smuggled-unversioned-field anti-pattern named in ADR section 11. Found by independent evaluation; from_dict now refuses unknown fields with an explicit required and optional split.
lesson: Every packet from_dict must reject unknown fields symmetrically; a permissive parser turns a field vanishing on round-trip into an invisible defect.

cause: A shared session limit terminated the Lane A and Lane D subagents mid-implementation.
impact: Two lanes stalled. Per ADR section 11 their work in progress was committed to preserve evidence, then both were resumed after the reset from the preserved commit and both reached green.
lesson: On a runner or session interruption, commit the interrupted lane's work in progress immediately so no work is lost and the lane can resume from a clean commit rather than restart.

impact: 29 real ETS evaluation cases fail at option validation instead of reaching estimation and diagnostic assertions; the seam cannot be called green.
lesson: Keep result-contract metadata separate from model-input options; a fail-closed pack must not accept fields that only belong to the output packet.

cause: The ETS result contract was upgraded with time_index_semantics, but the ETS input options and estimator did not carry that semantic through; a regular business-day fixture was therefore blocked as an irregular calendar series and successful results would default their identity back to regular_calendar.
impact: The real ETS evaluation cannot distinguish trading-observation spacing from a broken regular calendar, so the Notebook alternative is unusable on business-day data.
lesson: When a contract adds a semantic field, wire it through input validation, sample audit, result construction, and result identity before claiming the contract is implemented.

cause: The merged ETS canonical fixture is contract version 1.1 with n_excluded=0 and an exact BIC value, while the UI lane assertions still expected the earlier illustrative exclusion and rounded BIC values.
impact: The Notebook UI regression suite could not validate the ETS result packet after the lane merge; the assertions were repaired to the locked fixture without changing product values.
lesson: When a contract fixture changes in an integration branch, update consumer assertions to the canonical packet and never restore illustrative values to make a test green.

cause: The real Notebook browser path consumed the HTTP context packet, but NotebookPlanningContextV1.to_dict() did not expose generation_context_hash or freshness_dependency_fingerprint even though the option contract and UI require both fingerprints.
impact: The UI correctly refused to render a partially specified context slice, so the real Notebook route stopped at NOTEBOOK_LOAD_FAILED before showing options.
lesson: Browser-check the serialized boundary, not only the typed in-process context; every execution-gating fingerprint required by the UI contract must be present in the HTTP packet.

cause: The Notebook route effect set its active id and URL before marking the asynchronous initialization as handled, so the rerender could start a second create request while the first request was still loading its context.
impact: A fresh Notebook entry could create two notebooks and therefore two RunFamily identities before the user saw the surface.
lesson: Mark asynchronous route initialization as claimed before triggering state or URL updates; identity creation must be idempotent under React effect rerenders.

cause: The options snapshot endpoint serialized current_revision directly, but lifecycle transitions are append-only records folded separately by OptionView; after confirmation the immutable revision still says proposed even though the folded lifecycle is executing.
impact: Reloading a Notebook after confirmation displayed an executing option as proposed and lost the pending state, contradicting the lifecycle contract even though the append-only log was correct.
lesson: Every read projection must fold both immutable revision data and lifecycle/execution state; serializing the revision alone is not a current-state snapshot.

cause: The HTTP Notebook context packet now explicitly serializes both generation_context_hash and freshness_dependency_fingerprint required by the execution contract.
impact: The real HTTP Notebook route now supplies the two fingerprints needed for the UI context slice and execution gating.
lesson: Serialize every execution-gating fingerprint at the HTTP boundary and verify the browser-facing packet, not only the in-process object.

cause: The runless Notebook route claims initialization before async loading and URL state updates, preventing React effect rerenders from creating another notebook or RunFamily.
impact: Fresh runless Notebook initialization is idempotent under the React effect lifecycle used by the Workbench route.
lesson: Claim identity creation before triggering state or URL updates so asynchronous route initialization cannot duplicate the RunFamily.

cause: The Notebook options snapshot now folds the current OptionView lifecycle and freshness axes over immutable revision data before serializing the read response.
impact: Reloading a confirmed Notebook preserves the executing state instead of presenting the immutable proposed revision as current state.
lesson: Read projections must fold append-only lifecycle state over immutable revisions before crossing the HTTP boundary.

cause: The requested Codex-inspired interaction is implemented as an ephemeral floating selection toolbar with three primary actions and a typed source reference, while existing follow-up, note, and deferred-option actions remain available behind More actions.
impact: Selection actions now match the requested Add to task, More details, and Ask in side chat affordances without automatic send or analysis execution.
lesson: Treat selected text as an ephemeral UI anchor carrying a typed source ref; action handlers may prepare or route a question but must not bypass proposal validation or confirmation.

cause: The full backend gate reached the sandbox tests, but the current macOS host rejected sandbox-exec with 'sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted'; the contained execution process did not start.
impact: Full gate is not a release-pass signal on this host; focused Notebook, backend integration, golden, and frontend checks remain separately usable evidence.
lesson: Keep host capability failures distinct from product regressions and rerun the containment gate on a host that permits the required sandbox primitive before release acceptance.

cause: The approved Notebook direction requires Graph-bound projection, bounded raw-data evidence, and a service-layer gate that refuses to force a first recommendation when candidates are tied or evidence is insufficient.
impact: The current independent runless Notebook and deterministic hardcoded planner are not sufficient for evidence-backed recommendation or Graph-consistent execution provenance.
lesson: Treat recommendation rank as a validated evidence outcome, not as list order; preserve structured proposals without materializing unselected Graph branches.

cause: The Task 1 implementation subagent did not return a completion or blocker status after repeated bounded waits and two explicit completion requests, despite leaving a tested work-in-progress patch.
impact: Controller stopped the unresponsive worker, preserved the work-in-progress patch, and will perform explicit TDD verification, scope review, and commit before the required independent reviews.
lesson: Treat a silent implementation worker as a process failure: preserve its patch, stop it after bounded retries, and take over only with explicit verification and ownership boundaries.

cause: Task 1 replaced the public NotebookOptionRevision and OptionExecution constructors with v1.1-required fields before the planning/materialization tasks migrate current writers.
impact: The existing Notebook service cannot create legacy revisions: 17 focused Notebook regression tests fail with missing v1.1 evidence constructor arguments.
lesson: A versioned successor contract must preserve legacy public constructors and use an explicit parser or successor type until every write path is migrated atomically.

cause: The first Task 1 implementation preserved Python legacy writers but did not completely mirror Python legacy parsing and strict validation in TypeScript, and omitted several fail-closed tests.
impact: Task 1 cannot advance to code-quality review until TypeScript legacy defaults, numeric and source-pin parity, and required negative coverage are repaired and re-reviewed.
lesson: A cross-language contract lock must test legacy defaults and each rejection rule on both sides; green language-local fixtures are not proof of wire parity.

cause: A Task 1 worker staged complete frontend contract files that also contained pre-existing ETS and selection-interaction hunks outside Task 1.
impact: Controller stopped the worker, restored only those two index entries, then reconstructed the Task 1 staged patch while retaining all unrelated worktree edits.
lesson: When a shared dirty file has mixed ownership, verify the staged diff hunk-by-hunk and remove unrelated index changes before committing; a clean worktree diff is not enough.

cause: Python v1.1 parsing converted raw array fields before type validation and read version fields before validating Mapping input, creating non-fail-closed behavior absent from the TypeScript mirror.
impact: Task 1 cannot advance until bare strings are rejected for array fields and non-object input produces the unified contract error rather than AttributeError.
lesson: At a contract boundary, validate the raw container before conversion and validate the outer object before any field lookup; conversion-first parsing can manufacture valid-looking data from invalid wire values.

cause: The malformed-wire repair validated raw containers for several new tuple fields but still iterated evidence_refs before validating its outer container.
impact: Empty strings and mappings can be converted to an empty evidence tuple, so Task 1 remains blocked until evidence_refs is fail-closed on raw container type.
lesson: When repairing a conversion-before-validation class, enumerate every collection-bearing field and test each raw container boundary; analogous fields are not automatically protected.

cause: Task 1 completed compatibility, strict parsing, and cross-language contract validation after independent specification and quality review loops.
impact: Versioned Notebook option, recommendation, materialization, and execution packets are now a stable boundary for Task 2 persistence work.
lesson: Cross-language contract work should not close on focused fixtures alone; preserve legacy writers, test malformed wires, and require separate specification and quality approval.

cause: The Task 2 implementation agent did not report progress or leave its required red tests and source-projection patch after repeated bounded waits and a direct progress request.
impact: Controller stopped the agent before it changed scoped product files and will split Task 2 into narrower sequential sub-tasks while retaining the locked external behavior.
lesson: When a stateful persistence task spans identity, locking, and append-only records, reduce the worker scope to one testable state boundary instead of waiting on a silent broad implementation task.

cause: The source-projection implementation used per-store locks and treated any nonempty projection key as default, leaving cross-service duplication and invalid-key acceptance paths.
impact: Task 2A is blocked until default projection uniqueness is shared per project and every persisted default key is exact for its RunFamily.
lesson: Default identity invariants must be tested across independent service instances and validate the persisted key formula, not merely a nonempty key on one instance.

cause: The shared lock protected Dataset default creation but not first-time run migration and resolution; the new lock registry and concurrency test also lacked bounded lifecycle and wait behavior.
impact: Task 2A remains blocked until the complete run source identity sequence is project-locked and concurrency resources are bounded and diagnosable.
lesson: For source identity, lock the entire resolve-or-create decision before any migration write, and make lock registries and concurrency tests explicitly bounded.

cause: Task 2A source-bound default projection implementation passed its corrected cross-service identity and quality reviews.
impact: Task 2B may now add append-only Notebook state without reopening source identity or introducing a source-less default execution path.
lesson: Default projection identity requires source/key validation, project-shared locking across migration and creation, and bounded concurrency tests before dependent state persistence begins.

cause: Task 2B retained legacy lifecycle edges that allow selected options to execute without materialization and executing options to return to selected.
impact: Task 2B cannot pass specification review until execution is reachable only through materialized and executing has no selected edge.
lesson: Lifecycle tables must be tested for forbidden edges as well as intended happy paths, especially where an intermediate provenance record is mandatory.

cause: The lifecycle repair labeled confirmation materialized before any Draft or materialization record existed, while the append-only materialization store accepted records without binding them to a materializable current option and its Notebook family.
impact: Task 2B cannot close: a legacy option can gain a materialization record, and the Notebook can claim materialized before Graph Draft provenance exists.
lesson: A materialized lifecycle state must be written only after the matching Draft and provenance record exist, and low-level append APIs must validate their immutable foreign keys rather than trusting callers.

cause: The v1.1 lifecycle transition helper permits selected to materialized without first verifying the matching append-only OptionMaterialization record.
impact: The Notebook can persist a materialized lifecycle claim that has no materialization or Draft provenance, violating the graph-first invariant.
lesson: A provenance-dependent lifecycle state must validate the immutable provenance record at the state transition, and tests must reject the direct state path.

cause: The v1.1 lifecycle table allowed selected to materialized while the shared transition helper did not require a matching persisted materialization record.
impact: A v1.1 option could be labeled materialized without immutable materialization provenance, violating the Graph-first handoff boundary before Task 7 creates the real Draft.
lesson: Every transition into materialized must validate the corresponding immutable record; callers must not be trusted to have created it first.

cause: Task 2 validates a persisted OptionMaterialization record but its errors and tests described that record as a real PipelineDraft materialization before Task 7 implements Draft creation and verification.
impact: Task 2 would overstate record-level provenance as verified Draft existence and obscure the remaining Task 7 boundary.
lesson: Contract language must name the strongest fact actually verified at its layer; record linkage is not Draft existence.

cause: Task 2B now enforces record-level OptionMaterialization provenance for every new v1.1 transition into materialized, while keeping PipelineDraft existence explicitly in Task 7.
impact: Task 2 persistence now rejects legacy records, foreign/mismatched option pins, direct v1.1 confirmation, and materialized state without a bound persisted record; real PipelineDraft provenance remains an explicit Task 7 gate.
lesson: Materialization must advance in two explicit layers: Task 2 binds immutable Notebook provenance, then Task 7 creates and verifies the Graph Draft it names.

cause: Task 2B append-only evidence, decision, materialization-record, versioned lifecycle, and legacy isolation behavior passed corrected specification and independent quality reviews.
impact: Task 3 may bind the HTTP projection boundary to real Graph and Dataset sources while Task 7 remains solely responsible for real PipelineDraft creation and verification.
lesson: Record-level provenance, lifecycle gates, and legacy compatibility must be version-separated and independently reviewed before a later Draft materializer can rely on them.

cause: Several delegated workers did not begin their assigned bounded task or report progress within repeated observation windows, while the controller waited instead of immediately reclaiming the critical path.
impact: Repeated wait cycles produced no new code or test evidence and delayed Task 3. The critical path is now controller-owned; subagents are restricted to time-boxed review after a local validated slice exists.
lesson: Time-box delegated work to one observation window; if no concrete diff, test result, or blocker arrives, close it and reclaim the task rather than extending waits.

cause: The formal devline CLI imported workbench from the main checkout through the shared virtualenv path, so verification initially inspected a different development-control implementation and reported an untrustworthy event log.
impact: One verification attempt was invalid until PYTHONPATH=backend forced the active worktree package; no product files were changed by the failed check.
lesson: Run formal development-control commands with the active worktree package explicitly selected, and verify the imported module path before trusting process evidence.

cause: The first Task 4 regression run exposed two integration seams: the compiler ownership guard needed to recognize the new evidence compiler, and the freshness whitelist had to include the already shipped family comparison point plus persisted evidence references.
impact: The initial integration run was 56 passed and 2 failed; the ownership and freshness contracts were corrected, and the associated suite is now 58 passed.
lesson: When a second bounded compiler reads a registered source, update the structural ownership guard explicitly; when a new provenance ref enters context, update the declared freshness whitelist and its contract test together.

cause: Task 4 now provides a closed inspection registry, verified run/upload source resolution, bounded profile quality time-index sample and rolling-origin evidence, typed omissions and failures, append-only pack persistence, context evidence refs, and trace events.
impact: Task 5 may gate recommendation decisions on persisted, bounded Evidence Pack references; the evidence layer cannot create Drafts, Runs, Artifacts, or Graph mutations.
lesson: Evidence compilation must expose omissions and failures as typed records, persist the pack before context references it, and register trace schemas before recommendation logic consumes it.

cause: Task 5 now produces one batch-level RecommendationDecision, removes rank-based recommendation semantics, applies hard blocks before comparison, refuses incomplete or non-comparable evidence, and uses a declared protocol margin for empirical winners.
impact: Task 6 may replace the fixed planner with a typed provider adapter that submits options carrying evidence refs and consumes this single decision; tied and insufficient batches cannot claim a first choice.
lesson: Recommendation rank must be derived once at the batch boundary from hard and declared comparative evidence; option display order cannot be treated as a judgment.

cause: The first route integration assertion expected the symbolic contract name, while the locked wire contract serializes contract_version as the numeric value 1.1.
impact: One newly added integration test failed; product code and persisted records were not changed by the failed assertion.
lesson: Assert the locked public wire value from the contract module rather than re-deriving a symbolic display string in a route test.

cause: The new persistence assertion addressed the nested create response instead of the list-options route's flat option projection.
impact: One follow-up integration assertion failed; the stored v1.1 revision was already readable and the assertion was corrected to the public list projection.
lesson: When adding a persistence assertion, inspect the endpoint's documented projection shape before selecting nested response fields.

cause: The Trace registry already contained three evidence inspection event schemas, but the older twelve-event tests still asserted the pre-evidence registry and expected a non-inspecting decision chain to emit inspection events.
impact: The expanded Task 6 regression initially had 2 failures; tests now distinguish the core decision chain from the complete registry and pass 54 tests.
lesson: When a typed event registry expands, update exact-set tests and keep scenario tests responsible only for events they actually exercise.

cause: The first run-source materialization test used a hand-written graph payload that GraphStore could not deserialize and used a bare node hash where the family headset contract requires the composite forest key.
impact: The run rerun-child path could not reach the draft constructor; the dataset genesis path remained green. The fixture was repaired to use the real GraphStore model and composite forest key, and both materialization tests now pass.
lesson: Materialization fixtures must be built through the same GraphStore and forest-key conventions as the source-bound write validator; hand-written graph JSON is not an acceptable substitute for a valid lineage graph.

cause: The first HTTP materialization integration fixture returned an OptionDraft without the recommendation_decision_id and recommendation_status required by the v1.1 batch binding contract.
impact: The route correctly rejected the incomplete fake provider batch with OPTION_BATCH_DECISION_MISMATCH; the fixture was repaired to mirror the provider adapter and the materialize plus confirm-idempotency flow now passes.
lesson: HTTP planner fixtures must preserve the same batch-level decision binding fields as the real typed provider result; route tests should exercise the public contract, not a simplified pre-contract Option shape.

cause: After routing legacy Draft creation through the shared materialization constructor, the HTTP wrapper mapped typed source validation failures to the generic 422 path and changed SOURCE_NODE_HASH_MISMATCH from its established 409 response.
impact: One existing Draft API regression failed; no Draft was persisted. The thin wrapper now maps source mismatch and context errors back to their existing public status codes, and the compatibility suite is being rerun.
lesson: Shared domain constructors may centralize validation, but existing HTTP adapters must preserve their documented status and detail classification at the boundary.

cause: Task 7 now routes selected v1.1 Options through source-bound rerun-child or dataset genesis Draft constructors, preserves Draft API compatibility, and exposes idempotent materialize plus confirm-alias packets.
impact: Run and dataset materialization, stale and lifecycle gates, typed model.genesis capability, shared legacy Draft routes, HTTP materialize/confirm integration, and the combined Notebook regression are covered. No execution path was added and no Run is created for dataset genesis.
lesson: A materialization gate is only credible when both the new Notebook route and the old Draft entrypoints exercise the same constructor, while idempotency and compatibility are asserted at the HTTP boundary.

cause: A browser remount could retry the same provider batch, while proposal persistence always started the same option identity at revision one and appended a duplicate record.
impact: The duplicate made the materialization generation-context pin fail closed during browser acceptance; no Run was created and no invalid Draft was accepted.
lesson: Stable option identity must make identical proposal retries idempotent; never append a duplicate revision number.

cause: The authorized DeepSeek provider returned inspection and proposal payloads that violated the published typed Notebook contract: an unknown inspection id, missing evidence references in a comparative claim, and an unpinned dataset source.

evidence.ref: real DeepSeek bounded Notebook planning smoke

impact: The provider call failed with HTTP 422 and produced no recommendation, Draft, Run, or persisted numeric result; no fallback path was used and credentials were not written to the repository.
lesson: Provider prompts can improve compliance, but semantic source and evidence pins remain server-owned and must fail closed when the model omits them.

cause: The browser successfully materialized a dataset genesis Draft, but a route remount only reloaded option revisions and therefore dropped the in-memory materialization handoff from the Notebook surface.
impact: The Draft existed and no Run was created, but the UI failed to expose the Graph handoff after reload, making a valid persisted state appear incomplete.
lesson: Every persisted Notebook lifecycle transition must be returned by the public projection and hydrated by the route; local UI state cannot be the only record of a Draft handoff.

cause: The graph-bound Notebook path was exercised from a fresh zero-run project with an uploaded dataset, bounded evidence inspection, typed recommendation, user confirmation, genesis Draft materialization, and Draft Graph handoff.

evidence.ref: browser fresh project wb-v181-browser-20260723-0733; focused backend 189 passed; frontend 158 files 1367 tests passed

impact: The browser showed evidence-backed Recommended status, persisted Draft prepared, no Runs yet, and a disabled Execute Draft action; selected-text UI actions remain covered by frontend tests because the browser selection bridge is read-only for programmatic selection.
lesson: A graph-first Notebook acceptance must prove both the visible story and the absence of an unapproved Run; deterministic provider fixtures are appropriate for local UI QA when external provider output is not contract-clean.

cause: A bounded read-only reviewer was started after local verification but did not return findings within its allotted observation window.
impact: No product files were changed and no verification evidence was produced; the critical path was not extended after the timeout.
lesson: Use one bounded review window after a validated slice; reclaim the path when no concrete findings arrive instead of extending waits.

cause: A direct Graph reload without an active Run or notebook query did not reuse the project's sole persisted Notebook and instead showed zero-run onboarding.

evidence.ref: frontend/src/notebook/NotebookRouteView.notebook.test.tsx::reuses the sole persisted Notebook when Graph reload has no active Run

impact: A valid persisted Notebook could appear absent after navigation; no data or Run was mutated. The route now reuses exactly one persisted Notebook and refuses to guess when several exist.
lesson: Graph-bound Notebook routing must recover an existing single projection on reload; ambiguity across multiple projections must remain explicit rather than silently choosing a family.

cause: The authorized DeepSeek provider produced several semantically invalid but parseable Notebook proposals during bounded real smokes: invalid operation identity, incomplete genesis preconditions, unsupported genesis change fields, duplicate executable options, and an undeclarable required artifact.

evidence.ref: real DeepSeek bounded Notebook smoke plus 19 local provider/planning tests

impact: The earlier attempts remained fail-closed and created no unsafe Run or numeric result. The Agent boundary now rejects these payloads before persistence, provides at most two typed correction turns, and the final bounded smoke returned HTTP 200 with three persisted options; recommendation status remained insufficient_evidence and was not promoted.
lesson: Prompt and JSON Schema alone do not make a provider typed; the server must project operation and artifact contracts, validate them before persistence, and offer bounded correction without silently repairing model payloads.

cause: A real DeepSeek smoke after the first contract hardening still produced parseable option batches that omitted the runtime-required proposal_revision or used an unsupported proposal field shape; the generic operation schema also rejected legacy Analysis Loop compatibility payloads after unknown-change closure was tightened.

evidence.ref: real DeepSeek smoke: first option batch required two bounded corrections; post-fix smoke completed with HTTP 200 and 2 options; focused Notebook/Agent/Analysis Loop suite 181 passed

impact: Provider payloads remained untrusted and never reached persistence until they satisfied the strict boundary. The repair now makes proposal_revision mandatory in the advertised schema, names missing/unknown fields in correction feedback, closes model.rerun changes to explicit normal and legacy branches, and preserves the old Analysis Loop path without reopening arbitrary Notebook fields.
lesson: Every runtime-required typed field must be required in the provider-facing schema, and every rejection must identify the exact missing or unknown field; compatibility must be a named branch rather than a global additionalProperties escape.

cause: The user reran scripts/gate.sh --full in an unrestricted macOS Terminal after stopping the Vite preview; the real host run completed with 3459 backend tests passed, 3 backend failures, 8 skipped, 1 xfailed, 23 golden and invariant checks passed, and 158 frontend files with 1368 frontend tests passed.

impact: The sandbox-only refusal was removed, establishing a trustworthy host baseline. Three remaining failures were isolated to a false-positive producer capability probe, source-less Notebook planning error classification, and Draft project-not-found error preservation; no unsafe Run or numeric artifact was created.
lesson: A full gate must be rerun outside the restricted application sandbox when process contention or filesystem permissions affect the result, and its exact residual failures must become the next bounded repair set.

cause: The host gate exposed three residual contract seams: the evaluation probe treated a fail-closed Notebook producer placeholder as an available callable, source-less server planning entered evidence inspection before reporting planning unavailability, and the Draft HTTP wrapper flattened repository PROJECT_NOT_FOUND into generic 422.

evidence.ref: 52 focused tests passed with 1 intentional producer xfail; 851 Notebook, Agent, Context, Analysis Loop, Draft, RunFamily and v181 evaluation tests passed with 2 intentional xfails

impact: The evaluation lane now preserves the real missing-provider gap as strict-xfail, source-less planning returns NOTEBOOK_PLANNING_UNAVAILABLE before any evidence read, and unknown projects retain the canonical 404 PROJECT_NOT_FOUND response. No fallback producer, Run, or numeric result was introduced.
lesson: Importability is not implementation evidence when a public seam is intentionally fail-closed; domain exceptions carrying HTTP status must also survive thin route adapters without generic remapping.

cause: The user reran the full Workbench gate in an unrestricted macOS Terminal after stopping the preview server. Backend completed with 3461 passed, 8 skipped, and 2 intentional xfailed; golden and invariant checks completed with 23 passed; frontend completed with 158 test files and 1368 tests passed; TypeScript typecheck completed successfully.

evidence.ref: user-provided macOS Terminal full gate rerun ending with GATE PASSED

impact: The v1.8.1 implementation baseline is green under the real host gate. The two xfails remain explicit deferred seams rather than hidden failures, and golden values remain zero-drift.
lesson: A sandbox-blocked gate is not release evidence; repeat it on the host, record backend, golden, frontend, and typecheck results together, and preserve intentional xfails as visible scope boundaries.

cause: The provider-neutral model_options envelope was accepted by the typed operation registry even when the source model Draft editable schema did not declare model_options.
impact: DeepSeek proposals could fail late with NON_EDITABLE_PARAM and leave an orphan Draft. The materializer now preflights the source schema, rejects with OPTION_MATERIALIZATION_FAILED, and does not persist a Draft on failure.
lesson: A generic typed envelope must be checked again against the target Draft editable schema before any materialization write.

cause: The isolated browser fixture was exercised from a real completed Graph Run with a persisted source-bound RunFamily and bounded profile evidence.

evidence.ref: browser project wb-v181-browser-task9; Graph -> Notebook -> Option -> Draft -> Graph; deferred sibling retained; stale confirm returned HTTP 409 OPTION_REVISION_STALE

impact: The visible Notebook now shows materialized Draft handoff, deferred sibling lifecycle, and stale disabled execution gates without creating an unapproved Run.
lesson: Task 9 acceptance must record both the visible graph-first story and the service-level stale rejection code.

cause: The browser automation connector exposes DOM interaction but not real mouse selection, and Computer Use is not approved for the browser app in this session.
impact: The four selected-text actions are covered by real frontend interaction tests, but a manual OS-level drag selection could not be honestly claimed in this sandboxed session.
lesson: Keep component-level action evidence separate from browser-level native selection evidence; do not promote a test-only result to manual browser acceptance.

cause: The complete scripts/gate.sh --full run finished after the producer seam, provider transport recovery, genesis status, and Draft semantic preflight repairs.

evidence.ref: scripts/gate.sh --full: 3466 backend passed, 8 skipped, 1 xfailed; 23 golden/invariant passed; 158 frontend files and 1368 tests passed; TypeScript typecheck passed; GATE PASSED

impact: The v1.8.1 implementation is green under the complete gate with golden values at zero drift. Intentional xfail scope remains visible; no provider fallback, unsafe Run, orphan Draft, or numeric artifact was introduced.
lesson: After a bounded repair set, rerun the full gate and record backend, golden, frontend, and typecheck evidence together before declaring the implementation state green.

cause: The Notebook HTTP layer created a fresh TraceWriter on every compile, the frontend retained a stale proposed Option after Review, repeated selected decisions were not idempotent, and Genesis materialization rejected the valid OLS covariance field.

evidence.ref: focused RED reproduction: repeated selected returned 409, frontend retained proposed, covariance materialization failed; GREEN: Notebook backend 134 passed, frontend Notebook 74 passed, typecheck passed

impact: A browser remount could hide the planning decision chain, retrying Review could fail with OPTION_LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_INVALID, and a valid model.genesis proposal could fail before Draft creation. No Run or numeric artifact was created by the failures.
lesson: Notebook navigation state must be durable and request retries must be idempotent at the public operation boundary; materializers must validate against the published capability vocabulary without rejecting fields that the typed proposal contract legitimately carries.

cause: After persisting one Notebook trace, concurrent remount requests still constructed separate TraceWriter instances from the same replay length and wrote duplicate envelope sequence numbers.

evidence.ref: in-app browser reload showed preserved 15-event history; pre-repair concurrent append exposed duplicate sequence 16; focused trace regression passed

impact: The planning evidence was retained, but the old concurrent append could make displayed sequence numbers ambiguous. No Run or numeric artifact was affected.
lesson: A persisted trace identity also needs serialized sequence allocation; shared single-worker write coordination must cover replay, numbering, and append as one operation.

cause: The in-sandbox full gate could not invoke macOS sandbox-exec; every remaining backend failure returned sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted.

evidence.ref: scripts/gate.sh --full: 3447 passed, 8 skipped, 1 xfailed; 20 sandbox-only failures; golden/invariants 23 passed; frontend 158 files 1369 tests passed; typecheck passed

impact: The Notebook repair slice is green in focused and frontend checks, but this environment cannot provide the required host-level sandbox evidence. No product failure was observed outside the restricted macOS sandbox boundary.
lesson: Separate product regressions from host sandbox capability failures; retain the exact host command as the remaining acceptance step instead of weakening sandbox policy or changing tests.

cause: After Home to Workbench navigation dropped the notebook query parameter, the Notebook view preferred the focused Run and attempted to create a new projection instead of recovering the sole persisted Notebook.

evidence.ref: in-app browser Home -> Workbench -> Notebook: pre-fix POST /notebooks/projection returned 422; post-fix GET /notebooks and Notebook options/trace requests returned 200

impact: A persisted Dataset-backed Notebook could appear lost after navigation and the user could be prompted to upload again; no new Run or numeric artifact was created by the rejected request.
lesson: Recover a unique durable Notebook projection before deriving a new projection from the currently focused Run; view URL parameters are navigation hints, not the source of Notebook identity.

cause: An executed option could become stale after active-head advancement and was then evaluated by the freshness gate before its terminal lifecycle state.

evidence.ref: frontend/src/notebook/OptionCard.notebook.test.tsx: executed stale option remains terminal; frontend Notebook focused suite 25 passed

impact: The UI could offer Revalidate for an already executed option even though the lifecycle state machine correctly refuses another materialization or execution.
lesson: Evaluate terminal lifecycle actions before freshness so executed, rejected, and archived options remain closed even when their historical context is stale.

cause: The in-sandbox full gate again could not invoke macOS sandbox-exec; the remaining backend failures were sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted.

evidence.ref: scripts/gate.sh --full: 3456 passed, 8 skipped, 1 xfailed, 20 sandbox-only failures; frontend 158 files and 1380 tests passed; focused Notebook/backend checks passed

impact: The product regression slice remains covered, but this environment still cannot provide host-level macOS sandbox acceptance evidence. No Notebook Run or numeric artifact was created by the sandbox boundary failures.
lesson: Keep the host sandbox boundary explicit and rerun the prescribed full gate from a normal macOS Terminal; do not weaken sandbox policy or change tests to make the in-sandbox gate green.

cause: The VIXCLS Notebook provider produced unsupported flat model_options aliases for the time_series.arma_garch target, and the pre-persistence target-contract gate was not yet present in the running implementation.

evidence.ref: in-app browser VIXCLS Notebook EGARCH option persisted a flat model_options payload and Draft Execute ended in failed

impact: A Draft could be created and validated from a provider proposal that did not match the source model contract; execution produced no new analysis Run. The repair now rejects the proposal before Option persistence when a real source contract is available.
lesson: Generic Notebook planning must bind model_options to the target model's published owner contract before persisting an Option or Draft; unsupported aliases must be rejected rather than normalized by guesswork.

cause: The Notebook options route persisted execution_result records but did not project them to the browser, so a remount could show a completed Draft without the model-neutral Run and artifact-contract outcome.

evidence.ref: in-app browser VIXCLS Notebook reload showed the completed child Run in Run history but no generic execution result in the Notebook

impact: Different model families could execute successfully yet lose the durable Notebook result projection on navigation; the user would have to infer success from Graph or Run history. No numeric result was recomputed or fabricated by the projection.
lesson: A global Notebook must project persisted execution outcomes by Option revision and keep model-specific payloads in Run artifacts; reload must not depend on transient ETS or confirmation state.

cause: The genesis materializer gated the mandatory-x rule on a literal model_type comparison (model_type != time_series.arma_garch), so ETS, a univariate model with the identical capability shape and no x regressors, was wrongly required to supply non-empty x and could not materialize a genesis draft.
impact: A univariate model added in this wave (ETS) could not be run through the model-agnostic Notebook genesis path; every future univariate model would need to patch the same branch.
lesson: Derive model shape (whether X regressors are required) from the target capability's declared params (role==x, required), never from a hardcoded model_type literal; the Notebook is model-agnostic and must stay unpatched as models are added.

cause: The ETS declared_pack fixture mutated the model registry and declared the pack directly but left the loader tracking sets untouched, so build_capabilities re-invoked the loader, saw an untracked pre-registered handler and fail-closed; the test only passed when an earlier in-process loader bootstrap happened to prime that state, and it contaminated the LMM seam tests in a shared process.
impact: tests/models/ets was not independently runnable and knocked out 4 LMM seam tests when co-scheduled; a green-in-full-suite / red-in-isolation hazard that can mask a real double-registration regression.
lesson: A fixture that mutates shared registration state must restore every coupled registry together, including the loader tracking sets, so the test does not depend on hidden in-process ordering.

cause: Affected paths differ from the frozen Context Pack and require an explicit scope correction.
lesson: Record the exact old and new manifest identities before correcting development scope.

cause: An explicit Context Pack rescope replaced the affected-path snapshot.
lesson: Correct scope only through an audited, new frozen manifest generation.
